Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · Money, work & business

successful adjective

of a person: doing well in life, prosperous

also prosperous, thriving, flourishing, well-off, well-heeled

classical

Caes. BG 7.32: flōrentem et illūstrem adulēscentem
Cic. Fam. 2.13.2: hominem flōrentem aetāte, opibus, honōribus (Lewis & Short)

flōrēns, flōrentis

adjective, third declension, one ending (participle of flōreō)

flourishing, prosperous, successful

Of persons and states in their prime, rich in means, office or fame; the verb is flōrēre, to flourish.

Other words

  • fēlīx, fēlīcis — lucky, successful

    adjective, third declension, one ending · also used · classical · Cic. Rep. 2.9: bella cum fīnitimīs fēlīcissimē multa gessit (Lewis & Short)

  • beātus, beāta, beātum — happy, well off, prosperous

    adjective · also used · classical · Cic. Par. 18: quī tē beātum, quī flōrentem putās

  • bene aerātus — well-off

    avoid · modern · Traupman 159, 405

    We have found no instance of the phrase: Lewis & Short has aerātus, “furnished with money”, only in Cicero’s pun tribūnī nōn tam aerātī quam aerāriī (Att. 1.16.3). Say beātus or locuplēs.

Examples

  • tē miseriae, tē aerumnae premunt omnēs, quī tē beātum, quī flōrentem putās

    every misery and every trouble weighs on you, who think yourself happy and successfulCic. Par. 18

See also successful, poor.
